pk.context: 300 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

pill.desc: creamy-white to pale yellow, round extended-release tablet

tell: At steady state its hydroxybupropion metabolite peaks at about seven times the parent drug's level.

clues.text: Food does not affect its peak or AUC. It is 84% bound to plasma proteins and is extensively metabolized, with 87% of a dose recovered in urine.
The hydrochloride salt is a white, crystalline powder that is highly soluble in water. The active moiety has a molecular weight of 239.74.
Under an NDA, extended-release tablets of 150 and 300 mg, given once daily.

Boxed warning for suicidal thoughts and behavior in children, adolescents and young adults. Contraindicated in seizure disorder, bulimia or anorexia, and with MAOIs or abrupt withdrawal of alcohol or benzodiazepines.
Treatment of major depressive disorder, and prevention of seasonal affective disorder.
A relatively weak inhibitor of norepinephrine and dopamine reuptake that does not inhibit monoamine oxidase or serotonin reuptake.
The generic name begins with B and has nine letters.
